name: Symmetrical Cinematic Composition. This is a normalized label, derived from a Grand Budapest Hotel reference. The source notes that the result was not assessed by watching every source video.
visualIdentity: Explicit: the style uses axial symmetry, frontal framing, theatrical sets, and deliberately arranged props within a carefully selected palette. Measured lateral moves, push-ins, and ordered character actions carry the staging. Principles are adapted, not copied from a film scene or applied as a generic pastel filter.
suitableUses: Explicit: staged scenes, 3D dioramas and miniature sets, and balanced 2D illustration. Inferred: brand storytelling films and chapter-based narratives, based on the source's combination examples. Interactive HTML is explicitly mentioned only as pre-rendered frames scrubbed by scroll, not as a live interactive system.
limitations: The source says the style works alone for staged scenes. Symmetry must be maintained when combined with other styles, and oblique views should be avoided. Camera tilt that breaks symmetry or projection is unsuitable. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production. Stateful simulations must be prepared and cached first.
palette: Reference-dependent example, not a canonical style palette. Approved task or reference colors override it. Tokens: background #EEE0C8, foreground #39494B, accent_1 #8B9A81, accent_2 #B97D66. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background measures 7.239:1 and passes body text. Accents on foreground text fail (3.158 and 2.777), so they are decorative only. Verify composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Explicit: measured lateral moves, push-ins, and ordered character actions, using stable camera moves. Deliberate sharp cuts and reading holds are allowed, and not every transition needs easing. Interaction is unspecified for this style. Optional references motion-009, motion-012, and motion-015 are screened for fit, and selecting none is valid. Pointer or scroll input applies only to interactive delivery.
audio: Unspecified by the style, which assigns no fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer. Propose audio from the topic, audience, storyboard, and motion. Honor any explicit user or supplied audio first. Music, voiceover, sound effects, ambience, or silence are all options. Verify speech intelligibility, audio balance, absence of clipping, and synchronization with picture.
assetRequirements: For 3D, Blender models, materials, lighting, and animation are needed. For 2D, balanced illustration is needed. Exact copy and any supplied assets must be provided, otherwise they are unspecified. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Randomness must be seeded. Optional creature or miniature assets from motion-009 are needed only if the topic supports them.
combinations: Works alone. Suggested: style-079 for miniature diorama stages framed frontally, keeping axial symmetry and avoiding oblique views; HTML can use pre-rendered frames scrubbed by scroll. Suggested: style-052 for letterpress chapter cards with centered type and side light, avoiding deep bevels. Optional chapter handoffs may use motion-012 or motion-015 if they remain compatible.
productionApproach: Blender is the style_renderer and motion_engine, run through blender --background --python scene.py, with Cycles or EEVEE (confirm the engine identifier). HyperFrames is the primary pipeline, handling only composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when a documented limitation applies, and the reason must be recorded. Review opening, action, transition, and closing frames, and watch the full video.
